Jezow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Jeżów, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Jeżów began toward the end of the 18th century, growing from 27 (1793) to 455 by 1872; the town was home to 19th-century tzadik Jakow Landau, son of Awraham from Ciechanów. By 1921, 1,048 residents (39.5%) followed Judaism; a fall 1941 ghetto's 1942 liquidation sent most residents via the Warsaw Ghetto to Treblinka, with others dying from disease and starvation. Remarkably, 937 Jews were recorded in Jeżów by 1945, though this dropped sharply to just 25 by 1955. This cemetery, presumably established in the 1870s, saw local residents steal tombstones for construction and porch paving; the grounds were also used as pasture and farmland. In the early 1990s, Canadian Bernard Gold funded maintenance and a metal fence for the site.
